sections.heading: Default structure
sections.text: Boost PFC is the standard single-phase power factor correction topology. A three-loop structure: inner current loop shapes the input current to follow the rectified line voltage, outer voltage loop regulates the DC bus, and a multiplier generates the current reference from the voltage error and the line voltage waveform.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: Current-loop crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/10. Voltage-loop crossover: f_cv < 2*f_line/10 (~10-20Hz for 50/60Hz). The voltage loop must be slow enough to avoid distorting the current reference. RHPZ: f_RHPZ = R_load*(1-D)^2/(2*pi*L). At high line and light load, f_RHPZ is lowest.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: The 2*f_line ripple on the DC bus is inherent. If the voltage-loop bandwidth is too high, this ripple modulates the current reference, causing input current distortion (cross-over distortion). The voltage-loop compensator must have low gain at 2*f_line. Output capacitor sizing: C_out >= P_out/(2*pi*f_line*V_ripple*V_out).

sections.heading: Inrush limiting
sections.text: At startup, the output capacitor charges through the boost diode with no current limiting. Add an inrush limiting circuit (NTC relay or pre-charge MOSFET) or ramp the voltage reference during startup. The current loop must be enabled before the voltage loop reaches regulation.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If the PFC cannot meet THD or power factor specs: (1) increase current-loop bandwidth, (2) add feedforward of the line voltage, (3) consider interleaved PFC for lower current ripple. If efficiency is the issue, consider totem-pole PFC with GaN/SiC for bridgeless operation.
